articles.title: Acid Etched Glass
articles.summary: Even frosted satin surface, soft haze, no coarse flake, shown here in neutral grey; takes whatever colour you give it. Reads as your plain colour with a soft, even frosted-satin sheen; the mottle disappears and it looks like a clean satin or bead-blasted finish.
articles.what: Up close: Takes your colour. The paint is flat; the spec holds a fine, cloud-like mottle of roughness (R 102, std 11) about 10-30 px, with no metal and a gloss clearcoat, so it is a milky frosted-glass haze rather than any shape or grain you can see. From a distance: Reads as your plain colour with a soft, even frosted-satin sheen; the mottle disappears and it looks like a clean satin or bead-blasted finish. Measured spec (average): metal 23, roughness 102, coat 16. Shine: satin. Metal: none. It takes the colour you give the zone.
when: Fits: gt / sports car, show car, open wheel.
how: This finish is not listed in the Base Material picker, so you cannot pick it there.
Open the AI copilot (the ✦ AI button, bottom right) and ask for it by name, for example "put Acid Etched Glass on the hood".
Pick your colour with BASE COLOR.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Whole body: even frosted satin suits every panel
Hood and roof: soft reflections show on broad panels
Numbers read cleanly in any contrasting colour; there is no texture to interfere.
Almost any pattern: it is a clean frosted base
Pairs well with: chrome trim, gloss black, white, any accent colour.
Not listed in the picker: ask the AI copilot for it by name.
pitfalls: Not matte: roughness is around 100, so it still has a soft sheen
Not metal flake: sparkle is 0 and metal is none
Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, next to other loud finishes.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 23 (low metal, like carbon or subtle flake), roughness 102 (satin or eggshell), clearcoat 16 (maximum clearcoat).
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: Gloss shows the paint colour as it is, so any colour works; pick the colour for contrast with the neighbouring zones, not for the finish. Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, next to other loud finishes.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: almost any pattern: it is a clean frosted base; stripes and graphics: sit crisply on the satin
Patterns to avoid: glitter or flake patterns: break the clean frosted look
Spec overlays that work: gloss stripes over the frost: nice contrast of finishes; flake or pearl overlays at low strength for some life
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.
